architecture_goal.core: Core publishes self-describing typed evidence artifacts.
architecture_goal.knowledge_layer: KLC selects evidence by artifact_kind + schema_version and owns knowledge materialization outputs.
architecture_goal.runner: Runner records execution, retries and artifact registrations without defining evidence or knowledge semantics.

allowed_runner_responsibilities: orchestrate Foundation lifecycle without defining its contents
record attempts, timeouts, resource usage and failures
invoke KLC materializations and record their manifests
compose repository, workspace and portfolio execution scopes
contract.definition: Self-describing record of analysis execution and produced typed evidence artifacts. Runner owns lifecycle, process, retry and artifact registration; Core owns evidence semantics; KLC owns knowledge materialization semantics.
forbidden_runner_responsibilities: define evidence semantics from task_id, suite_id, profile_id or output path
rewrite unsupported evidence into a different schema
publish a knowledge capability merely because a Task was requested
hide analyzer or materialization failures behind fallback execution

analyzer_executions.semantic_rule: request provenance never defines artifact meaning

lifecycle.failure_rule: Missing or unsupported evidence is explicit; no hidden fallback or silent reinterpretation.
lifecycle.retry_rule: Every attempt is preserved; successful retry does not erase prior failure provenance.

materialization_executions.ownership_rule: Runner records execution references; KLC defines inputs, outputs, coverage and capabilities.

gaps: does not enumerate requested or executed public analyzers
does not register general evidence artifacts by artifact_kind and schema_version
Foundation reference records path/request only and not a validated Foundation fingerprint
non-SQL evidence semantics remain delegated to the Core repository manifest and file layout
retry attempts are not represented for direct profile execution
strengths: records repository revision and run fingerprint
records Core process lifecycle, timeout and resource diagnostics
validates and records typed sql-analysis/v1 metadata when SQL is selected

gaps: does not record repository revision/content fingerprint directly
does not enumerate public analyzers executed inside each profile
does not register typed evidence artifacts produced by each analyzer
task_id and task output directories remain the practical artifact-discovery boundary
capabilities are copied from downstream manifest but current KLC production remains partly Task-coupled
strengths: records shared Foundation schema and artifact fingerprint
records ordered Task composition, profiles, process summaries and all retry attempts
records downstream suite KLC materialization manifest and capabilities

gaps: typed evidence is not aggregated into one workspace artifact registry
analyzer and Foundation identities are indirect through nested repository/suite manifests
workspace completion does not itself prove required evidence availability for a materialization
suite-mode semantics inherit task_id-coupled artifact discovery
strengths: records selected repository set and analysis contract
links every repository profile or suite execution
records workspace KLC output and tool versions
preserves selected repository revision data in the resolved selection manifest

gaps: reuses the suite manifest schema for a specialized non-suite result
selects portfolio topology evidence through task_id=portfolio-topology
does not expose a typed repository-interface-catalog evidence registration
profile and artifact identities are incomplete on failed results
strengths: preserves per-repository clone/analysis failure stage and code
uses a compact repository result suitable for partial portfolio completion

explicitly_deferred: broad removal of all task_id routes before typed evidence exists
universal evidence envelope implementation for every current stage
caching, DAG execution and suite-local reuse
planning_conclusions.main_finding: Runner already records lifecycle and retries reasonably well, but it cannot yet tell KLC what evidence exists without Task/profile/file-layout knowledge. The missing runtime boundary is a typed evidence artifact registry, not another redesign of Task or Suite.

revised_sequence.reason: Use one generic Runner-owned audit to compare KLC knowledge requirements with Core evidence capabilities; begin with code-declared-data-model.
Define only complete raw type, field, relationship, inheritance and gap evidence required by the first independent knowledge type.
Core publishes typed code-declaration evidence and Runner registers it in analysis_execution_result/v1 without universalizing all analyzers.
KLC imports typed code declarations by artifact_kind + schema_version and removes the matching legacy data-model Task semantics.
Compare only code-declared model semantics, switch consumers for that knowledge, and remove the corresponding legacy umbrella path without compatibility adapters.
Add persistence mapping only after code-declared and physical models exist as independent knowledge.
Build the effective model last from independent KLC models while preserving source-layer provenance.

what_this_contract_does_not_solve: It does not define the payload fields needed to rebuild the conceptual model.
It does not make current Core outputs independent evidence artifacts.
It does not remove task_id routing from KLC by itself.
It does not justify a generic all-analyzer runtime refactor before the first materialization slice is understood.

purpose: Runner-owned target execution-result contract and current runtime-manifest gap assessment.
